A.biggest_strength: True open-ended exploratory sandbox with live arbitrary parameter controls (continuous learning rate and start position sliders), 4-decimal exact arithmetic, and animated playback.
A.biggest_weakness: Missing the standard viewport meta tag, causing mobile browsers to render the page as an unreadable, zoomed-out desktop canvas.

B.biggest_strength: Masterful progressive disclosure through 5 stepped scenes with coordinated color-coding connecting formulas, table columns, tangent lines, and parameter-axis step vectors.
B.biggest_weakness: Premature convergence artifact caused by cumulative two-decimal rounding, leading to the false claim that a learning rate of 0.3 'lands on 3' in finite steps.
factual_errors: Scene 3 claims that the 'about right' learning rate (η = 0.3) 'lands on 3'. Gradient descent with a constant learning rate of 0.3 on L(w) = (w - 3)² approaches 3 asymptotically and never reaches 3 in finite steps; it only reaches 3.00 here because the page rounds intermediate values to two decimal places at each iteration.

structured_output.reasons: Page B is the overall winner because its progressive 5-scene structure and visual scaffolding are far superior for educational course notes. While Page A offers a great sandbox with exact live math, it fails critically on mobile due to a missing viewport meta tag and does not visually illustrate the horizontal step vector along the parameter axis. Page B visually grounds the gradient descent mechanism through color-coded formulas, tangent lines, and directional step arrows, provides rich course notes on curvature stability and multi-dimensional training, and renders cleanly on mobile devices.
